questions.q: Which statement about escalators and accessible circulation is most accurate?

Accessible elevators are prohibited near escalators

questions.n: Escalators are not a universal accessible route; an appropriate accessible alternative such as an elevator or compliant ramp must be provided where required.

questions.q: Why are the top and bottom landing zones important?

They are used only for HVAC ducts

questions.n: Landing zones are critical transition areas and house comb plates, step leveling paths, safety devices, and drive/return components depending on the end.

questions.q: A parallel escalator arrangement generally places escalators:
o: At right angles on every floor
Side by side in the same general orientation
questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.

questions.q: The comb plate is located near:

The middle of the truss only

questions.n: The comb plate's teeth mesh with the step grooves at entry/exit landings to provide a transition between moving and stationary surfaces.

questions.q: For architecture review, escalators should be studied together with:
o: Passenger circulation, accessibility, structural openings, fire/life safety and energy controls

questions.n: Escalators are multidisciplinary building-utility elements whose performance and location affect architecture, structure, accessibility and life safety.

questions.q: Which planning statement is most accurate?
o: Elevators are always slower than escalators
Escalators are especially effective for continuous movement between adjacent or nearby levels, while elevators are better for direct service to many separated floors
Escalators are universally accessible to all users
Escalators can stop at any arbitrary floor without separate units
questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
questions.n: Escalators are continuous-flow devices generally connecting adjacent levels; elevators can provide selective floor-to-floor service over greater vertical ranges.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the moving handrail?
o: Provide passengers a moving support synchronized approximately with step travel
questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
questions.n: The handrail gives users a stable handhold while traveling on the moving steps.

questions.q: Why must an architect coordinate escalator floor openings early?
o: Openings can be located after construction with no consequence

questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
questions.n: Escalator placement affects slabs, beams, atria, headroom, landings, support points and circulation patterns.

questions.q: Why are escalators common in shopping centers and transit facilities?
o: They can travel to any nonadjacent floor without intermediate space
They provide continuous high-throughput passenger movement between adjacent levels
questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
questions.n: Escalators continuously move passengers and work well for sustained flows between nearby levels.

questions.q: An escalator is best described as:

questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.

questions.q: The return station is generally associated with:
o: The end where the step chain reverses direction around its return path
questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
questions.n: The step chain circulates in a closed loop, reversing around end assemblies at the landings.

questions.q: A crisscross escalator arrangement is characterized by:
o: All escalators moving in exactly the same direction side by side
Alternating escalator directions/positions between successive floors to create a compact circulation path
One escalator located outdoors with no landing
questions.ref: Standard escalator and moving-walk engineering terminology and conventional component functions.
questions.n: Crisscross arrangements alternate direction between floors and can encourage continuous movement through adjacent floor areas.
